traditionalDress.men: A simple kurta or shirt with a dhoti or loose trousers for everyday wear; a white kurta-dhoti with a turban is worn for the Shigmo festival.
traditionalDress.women: The Kunbi saree, a checked cotton saree traditionally worn by the indigenous Kunbi community, draped just below the knee; Goan Catholic women traditionally wear the Pano Bhaju, pairing a wrap-around lower garment with a lace-trimmed blouse — a blend of Indian and Portuguese styles.

festivals.name: Goa Carnival
festivals.description: A colorful pre-Lenten festival introduced during Portuguese rule, featuring parades, floats, music, and dancing in the streets over several days.

festivals.name: Shigmo
festivals.description: A spring folk festival honoring the arrival of the season and the homecoming of warriors, marked by processions, the Ghode Modni (horse dance), and other traditional performances.

festivals.name: Sao Joao
festivals.description: A monsoon festival where locals, especially young men, jump into wells, ponds, and rivers to celebrate the arrival of the rains, accompanied by singing and feasting.

folklore: Sateri, worshipped in the form of an anthill, is one of Goa's oldest folk deities and is venerated as a primordial mother goddess in villages across the state; over time she became closely associated with Shantadurga, a form of Durga especially popular in Goa.
